items.synopsis: The sysd process crashes with error logs upon exceeding its memory limit
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved platforms with telemetry streaming configured, the sysd (System Daemon) process crashes on the backup RE (Routing Engine), and error logs are observed when sysd memory usage continues to grow over time, and the memory limit is exceeded. This issue is observed when the 64-bit sysd consumes more memory than the configured system limit when the device has been running for a long time (typically more than 100 days) in the dual RE scenario.

items.synopsis: PPPoE session scale from 131K to 384K in a SVLAN subscriber model
items.description: On certain MX platform, there is an issue in scaling PPPoE sessions from approximately 131K to 384K when operating in an SVLAN subscriber model.

items.synopsis: JDI-RCT:M/Mx: : NGMVPN multicast traffic gets dropped post Change route-distinguisher/route-target on L3VPN instances.
items.description: Not consistent issue and happens when RD and RT change is done in all routing instances while the traffic is running. Also sometimes issue seen only in certain instances. When issue happens there will be traffic drop for inclusive tunnel and affecting all flows on inclusive tunnel and it may not recover unless some external events like route change occurs.

items.synopsis: BGP session teardown due to incorrect 'prefix-limit maximum exceeded' error when RIB sharding is enabled
items.description: On all Junos and Junos OS Evolved platforms, when prefix-limit or accepted-prefix-limit is configured under family route-target with rib-sharding, prefix-limit will be incorrectly reported as 'prefix-limit maximum is exceeded'. This causes the BGP session to go down immediately. This occurs because the system incorrectly counts each received route multiple times (once for the main thread and once for each shard)

items.category: Track PRs in BGP Flow Spec area & is part of BGP inside RPD.
items.synopsis: BGP IPv6 Flow Specification Session Flapping When inet6-flow Is Enabled
items.description: In certain Junos OS releases, BGP sessions may repeatedly reset when IPv6 Flow Specification (inet6-flow) is enabled. This behavior occurs when the router receives specific IPv6 Flow Specification updates that include a default (wildcard) match. Earlier releases do not exhibit this behavior, leading to a difference in observed stability when upgrading.

items.synopsis: On-Change telemetry mode missing notifications for BGP Ext-Comm updates
items.description: On Junos OS and Junos Evolved OS platforms, with on_change streaming telemetry subscription mode enabled, if a change is made on a BGP (Border Gateway Protocol) external community (ext-comm), the telemetry on_change module does not generate an update.

items.category: PFE L2 forwarding features on BT based platforms
items.synopsis: On PTX EVO platforms in EVPN-VXLAN scenario traffic will not egress out of the irb next-hop when the bridge-domain doesn't have VXLAN VNI configured
items.description: On all PTX Evolved platforms that support EVPN-VXLAN (Ethernet VPN-Virtual Extensible LAN), when the PTX router acts as a MAC-VRF (Media Access Control - Virtual Routing and Forwarding) EVPN gateway, it will fail to forward traffic routed through the 'irb' interface due to packets being discarded at PFE (packet forwarding Engine), causing packet loss.

items.synopsis: Abnormal termination of evo-cda-bt process could lead to node reboot of PTX
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved, PTX10004, PTX10008 and PTX10016 with LC-1202 inserted the device reboots if the evo-cd-bt crashes. This process could crash due to a timing issue.

items.synopsis: Traffic loss observed when restart routing is performed on L3VPN BGP-LU setup
items.description: On PTX10001-36MR, PTX10008 and PTX10016 Junos platforms, when preserve-nexthop-hierarchy is configured and restart routing is performed, then ipv4/ipv6 Layer 3 Virtual Private Network(l3vpn) traffic going over Border Gateway Protocol (BGP)-Labelled Unicast (LU) path may get dropped on downstream routers due to next hop not getting updated properly.

items.synopsis: The evo-aftmand process crash is observed post device restart due to the presence of a faulty PFE
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved PTX10002-36QDD, PTX10004 and PTX10008 platforms with LC1301 line cards, when a device restart is performed while one or more PFE (Packet Forwarding Engine) instances are in a faulty state, the faulty PFE state causes memory corruption post restart. This results in the evo-aftmand process crash and disruption of traffic forwarding.

items.category: Express PFE Load Balance for BX platforms
items.synopsis: The evo-aftmand process crash is observed following FPC restart
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved PTX10002-36QDD and PTX10004, PTX10008 platforms with LC1301 line card, when the FPC(Flexible PIC Concentrator) is restarted in high-scale environment, the evo-aftmand process crashes and generates a crash file due to missing validation checks for invalid forwarding next-hop information after restart. This leads to traffic disruption.

items.synopsis: Traffic dropped after priority change in VRRP with EVPN-VxLAN scenario
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms, in Virtual Router Redundancy Protocol (VRRP) with Ethernet Virtual Private Network - Virtual Extensible Local Area Network (EVPN-VXLAN) scenario, when VRRP priority is changed, the VRRP virtual Media Access Control (MAC) address can remain pinned as a static entry on the remote device. As a result, MAC movement does not occur correctly, and VRRP packets are dropped on the leaf device. This impacts VRRP operation after priority changes.

items.category: Host path software for ACX platform
items.synopsis: Error messages are seen on Junos OS Evolved ACX and QFX platforms
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved ACX and QFX platforms, when "set system ddos-protection protocol " is configured or ddos-protection configuration is deleted or when "show ddos-protection protocol" is executed then below logs will be seen.DDOS:POLICE: DdosPolicer does not exist DDOS:POLICE: Ddos group does not exist.

items.synopsis: VPLS Layer 2 multicast traffic might be duplicated after output traffic control profile or HCOS interface configuration changes
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved ACX platforms, when HCOS (Hierarchical Class of Service) and class of service are enabled for VPLS (Virtual Private LAN Service), deactivating and reactivating the output-traffic-control-profile or making HCOS interface configuration changes might cause L2 (Layer 2) multicast traffic to be duplicated toward the access interface.

items.synopsis: Underlay traffic interruption due to nexthop HOLD state triggered by delayed ARP refresh
items.description: On all Junos Evolved ACX platforms, underlay traffic is interrupted when ARP(Address Resolution Protocol) request packets required for refresh are dropped due to congestion or ratelimiting conditions. As a result, the nexthop entry temporarily transitions to a HOLD state in hardware even though ARP later recovers in the control plane. Traffic resumes only after the forwarding state is refreshed.

items.synopsis: PyEZ Issue, failing on RPC request "show arp interface <>" to EVO platforms
items.description: On all Junos Evolved platforms, on invalid interface fetching, display error is seen on "show arp interface <>" command.

items.synopsis: Prolonged commit time with largescale lo0 filter binds cause configuration load failure
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved platforms, commit operations with ~38005000 lo0 filter binds take ~4m42s (vs <1m expected). If commit exceeds 5 minutes, mgd times out, which cause configuration load failure and service impact.

items.category: EVO Netstack Juniper Tunnel Driver Module
items.synopsis: The LDP session does not come up when an IPsec SA is configured under OSPFv3
items.description: On Junos Evolved platforms, when Open Shortest Path First version 3 (OSPFv3) Internet Protocol Security (IPsec) SA is applied at the interface (IFD/IFL) level, Label Distribution Protocol (LDP) is able to discover the neighbor via User Datagram Protocol (UDP) Hellos, but fails to bring up the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) session, preventing the LDP session from becoming operational. Disabling the OSPFv3 IPsec SA immediately restores normal LDP operation. During the service impact, the session will be down and traffic will not be send. Once the LDP session comes up, traffic can be routed through it.

items.synopsis: RTC time sync delay after reboot on Junos OS Evolved platforms
items.description: On all Junos OS Evolved platforms, due to linux kernel issue, periodical sync from system time to RTC (Real-Time Communication) every 11min stops working when system time moves to backwards.

items.synopsis: Management access via telnet disconnects under certain conditions
items.description: On All Junos Evolved platform, management access via telnet disconnects under certain conditions.

items.synopsis: Rescue Configuration Check Fails
items.description: On all Junos OS Evolved ACX platforms, that cannot verify the syntax and integrity of the saved rescue configuration file when performing a configuration check.

items.synopsis: SNMP traps related to optics/optic's media lane alarms will not be raised
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved platforms, SNMP(Simple Network Management Protocol) management systems do not receive related to optics or transceiver lane and module alarm traps.

items.synopsis: ARP resolution failure for /32 static host routes via IRB in EVPN virtual-switch routing instances
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms that support EVPN (Ethernet VPN) virtual-switch routing instances, ARP (Address Resolution Protocol) resolution fails for static host routes configured with a /32 mask when the next-hop interface is an IRB (Integrated Routing and Bridging) interface and the destination host resides in a different subnet. As a result, ARP entries are not installed, MAC (Media Access Control) addresses of destination hosts are not learned, and traffic destined to those hosts becomes unreachable, causing service impact.

items.synopsis: The FPC crashes when VLANs on an AE interface are updated or deleted
items.description: On all Junos OS Evolved PTX Series platforms with multiple VLANs on an Aggregate Ethernet (AE) interface and an Firewall filter with family ethernet switching and bandwidth policer attached to both the AE interface and its associated VLAN interfaces, a modification or deletion of the VLANs will lead to a FPC crash. All the traffic over the affected FPC will be dropped.

items.category: Enhanced Broadband Edge support for firewall
items.synopsis: FPC crash occurs after configuration changes are made to a service-filter on specific MX platforms
items.description: FPC crash and aftd-trio core-dump will be observed on MX platforms supporting MPC10E, MPC11E, LC9600 line cards, and MX304 after configuration changes were made to a service-filter which was in use by BBE subscribers.

items.synopsis: CRC errors and packet loss are being observed at the peer device when using 1G fibre optic connections
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved ACX7509, ACX7348, ACX7332, and ACX7100-32C platforms with 1G fibre Optics, when the Inter-Packet Gap (IPG) setting intermittently falls below the IEEE minimum requirement of 8 bytes, and traffic passes through the PHY, certain receiving devices are sensitive to this reduced IPG, which leads to CRC (Cyclic Redundancy Check) errors and packet loss on the peer device connected to 1G fibre optics connection.

items.synopsis: Jdhcpd cores generated after upgrade
items.description: jdhcpd cores seen after upgrade with dhcpv6 for IANA/PD

items.synopsis: Insert command not working for "dhcp-local-server group" hierarchy
items.description: Insert command not working for "dhcp-local-server group" hierarchy, below error is seen: user@host# insert system services dhcp-local-server group servers-1 after syntax error, expecting `after' or `before'. user@host# insert system services dhcp-local-server group servers-1 bef syntax error, expecting `after' or `before'.

items.category: Issues related to Junos licensing infrastructure
items.synopsis: Snmp license polling cause license-check service crash
items.description: On Junos platforms, a race condition occurs when the Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) poller attempts to retrieve device license information while subscriber management and SNMP policing features are in use. This condition causes the license-check process to encounter a null pointer and generate a core dump. There is no traffic or service impact. However, license information retrieval through SNMP polling fail until the license-check service recovers.

items.synopsis: PFE crash due to memory corruption when STP is enabled
items.description: On all Junos Platforms, a rare memory corruption condition may occur in the Packet Forwarding Engine (PFE) when Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) is enabled and operating in default (distributed) mode. When the issue is triggered, the PFE crashes and a dc-pfe core file is generated. The exact trigger for the memory corruption is currently unknown.

items.synopsis: Repeated bbe-smgd crashes caused when the system issues a dynamic profile add request during PPPoE session creation, but receives a delete event before the add completes on MX platforms.
items.description: On all MX platforms where Enhanced Subscriber Management (bbesmgd) is enabled, activating PPPoE (PointtoPoint Protocol over Ethernet) over L2TP (Layer 2 Tunneling Protocol) triggers repeated crashes of the bbesmgd process, resulting in core dump generation. This issue affects both Junos and Junos EVO platforms.

items.synopsis: The L2Circuit traffic which are resolving over BGP-LU get drop when 'chained-composite-next-hop' for BGP-LU and 'preserve-nexthop-hierarchy' is configured
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms supporting 'chained-composite-next-hop' for BGP-LU (Border Gateway Protocol - Labeled Unicast), when having L2Circuit (Layer 2 Circuit) links configured, with indirect next-hop resolving on BGP-LU prefix, if 'chained-composite-next-hop' enabled for BGP-LU and with 'preserve-nexthop-hierarchy' configured, L2Circuit traffic will get dropped due to failure in installing the forwarding next-hop with labels for L2Circuit service.

items.synopsis: SCFD flow variation leads to error messages or process crash
items.description: On all Junos MX platforms with line cards MPC10/11/LC9600/LC4800, this includes the MX304 and SCFD (Suspicious Control Flow Detection) enabled, when there are numerous flows being added, deleted, or modified simultaneously, the system experiences error messages or process crashes due to thread synchronization issues. The process crash will cause the FPC to restart.

items.synopsis: I2C alarm and traffic drop is seen with a type of QSFP on certain ACX platforms
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved ACX7100-32C, ACX7100-48L, ACX7100-32C-K and ACX7100-48L-K platforms when QSFP-100G-FR optics which has serial number starting with 2J4 is plugged in, it is observed that the port goes down with I2C(Inter-Integrated Circuit) access failure alarm and traffic is dropped.

items.synopsis: Incorrect optics module fault triggered due to transient I2C read error
items.description: On all Junos OS Evolved platforms and MX platforms with MPC11, LC9600, LC4800 line-cards and MX304, The system encountered a momentary I2C communication issue while reading information from the optics module.Instead of treating it as a brief, recoverable read problem, the software incorrectly classified it as a hardware failure and prematurely marked the optics module as faulty.

items.synopsis: The rpd process will crash due to memory leak
items.description: The rpd process will crash due to a memory leak when configuration using apply-groups or ephemeral database for "routing-options autonomous-system independent-domain".

items.category: PFE L2 forwarding features on BT based platforms
items.synopsis: IRB routed traffic is dropped when both hosts are learned on the same SP-style Layer 2 interface on EVO-PTX platforms
items.description: On all Junos OS Evolved PTX platforms, IRB (Integrated Routing and Bridging) routed traffic is dropped when both source and destination hosts are reachable through the same Service Provider (SP)-style Layer 2 IFL (Logical Interface) and associated IRB interface.

items.synopsis: PFE might become unresponsive with scaled firewall filters configured
items.description: On PTX Series platforms running Junos OS Evolved, the Packet Forwarding Engine might become unresponsive when scaled firewall filters using TCAM-based match conditions are configured, which can delay the installation of new firewall filters

items.synopsis: High CPU utilization in EvoAftManBx process due to large FFT firewall filters exceeding TCAM limits
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved PTX10001/PTX10003/PTX10008/PTX10016/PTX10004/PTX10002-36QDD platforms and Line cards LC2101/PTX10K-LC1301-36QD, High CPU utilization (up to ~99.9%) is observed in the EvoAftManBx-mai process when large firewall filters with extensive range-based match conditions are applied, particularly using Fast Filter Table (FFT). When FFT hardware limits (~4K TCAM entries) are exceeded, the filter compilation falls back to Flexible Lookup Table (FLT), leading to excessive rule expansion and repeated FFT-to-FLT compilation attempts, resulting in sustained high CPU usage and continuous compilation loops causing taffic to be impacted.

items.synopsis: jdhcpd.re.re0 cored at trace_file_close_internal (traceptr=0x7efc443b2bb0) at ../../src/junos_trace.c:188
items.description: When DHCP trace options are enabled, there is a possibility that jdhcpd could core. In general, traceoptions should be enabled only for debugging. They should be disabled once debuffing is done.

items.synopsis: RE may fail to assign a default source address to traffic in a route table with no configured lo0 address

items.category: Issues related to EVO dependency layer including object graphs, incompletes, anomalies and nkdb
items.synopsis: The cosd process might crash after multiple commit and rollback operations
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved platforms, the cost daemon may crash and generate a core file due to an incorrect order on infrastructure notifications. When this occurs, the Class of service (CoS) application may fail to retrieve the required EVO object state, resulting in an application crash. The issue has been observed during configuration rollback and reapplication involving OSPF and RSVP configurations, but it may also occur with CoS configuration changes that trigger a similar internal notification sequence. When the issue occurs, the cost process generates a core dump and automatically restarts, after which normal operation resumes.

items.description: DNS resolution for traceroute does not work for a router using the mgmt_vrf with 23.4R2-EVO

items.description: Observing arpd.re core on dut with bt __pthread_kill_internal testcase teardown with version 25.2R2.8-EVO.

items.synopsis: Dropping packets on PTX PE from any ingress PE device adds padding to IPv6 packets going over MPLS L3VPN
items.description: On all Junos Evolved PTX series platforms, when acting as egress PE router, it drops padded packets from any ingress PE device. When this occurs, the packets that are discarded are padding to small IPv6 packets going over MPLS L3VPN. If the padding is removed, they are forwarded as expected.

items.description: On MX platforms with MPC10/MPC11/LC9600/LC4800 linecards and MX304/MX301 platforms, if SCFD (Suspicious Control Flow Detection) is enabled and lot of flow are tracked on the device, error logs may be reported when the table overflows. This is purely a display issue.
